basis: Localized skin fragility and palmoplantar blistering; episodic neuropathic symptoms do not establish nerve damage; oral erosions occur in <30%.
CNS tumour arising from specialized ependymocytes; hydrocephalus and central visual disturbances do not establish intrinsic eye or endocrine damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; ocular abnormalities include strabismus in 3/3 assessed and cataract in 1/1. Other organ findings are isolated in this small cohort.
Chronic lacrimal gland disease; an infectious or autoimmune cause is not established.
Squamous cell carcinoma originating in the tongue, an oral gastrointestinal structure.
Defined by severe cerebral, cerebellar and brainstem malformations together with cleft palate, an oral structural defect.
Neurologic disorder with alternating paralysis, seizures and intellectual disability; weakness does not establish primary muscle disease.
Lysosomal storage disorder; neurodegeneration, hepatic storage and skeletal dysplasia are common (approximately >=30% each). Variable cardiac and renal manifestations omitted at cap.
Premalignant keratinocyte lesion confined to skin; later carcinoma risk adds no organ.
Classified as a congenital anomaly syndrome with intellectual disability; supplied evidence does not establish common damage to additional organs.
Acute myeloid neoplasm of marrow and blood cells; leukemia alone does not establish an infectious or immune mechanism.
Congenital shortening, fusion and contractures of digits; reproductive anomalies have no axis, and nail abnormalities occur in <30%.
Primary T-cell immunodeficiency; recurrent respiratory and gastrointestinal infections are secondary, separately diagnosed diseases; other organ injury is uncommon.
Benign neoplasm originating in the thyroid, an endocrine gland.
Corneal dystrophy with scarring, erosions and progressive visual impairment; definition explicitly excludes systemic manifestations.
Primary syphilitic infection producing a localized indurated, eroded cutaneous or mucocutaneous sore.
Non-syndromic fusion of tibia and fibula with associated limb and joint deformity.
Defined chiefly by cerebral small-vessel disease and brain injury; damaging ocular and systemic findings vary across subtypes; retinal tortuosity alone is insufficient.
Defining microcephaly/developmental disability, congenital cardiac malformations and skeletal hypoplasia; additional organ abnormalities lack established common frequencies.
Congenital skeletal myopathy with scoliosis; eyelid dysfunction/ptosis in 4/4 assessed. Respiratory insufficiency and renal abnormalities occur in 1/5 each.
PTH resistance disorder; cataract and dental enamel hypoplasia each occur in 30-79%. Renal hormone resistance does not establish intrinsic kidney injury.
Anatomically defined umbrella for upper digestive tract disease; no additional mechanism or organ applies across the group.
Cataracts, intellectual disability and anal atresia define the syndrome; urinary tract malformations, including rectovesical fistula and hypospadias, are also defining.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis; middle-ear ciliary dysfunction manifests as recurrent otitis in 9/12 (~75%). Situs inversus alone adds no damaged organ.
Metaphyseal chondrodysplasia establishes skeletal disease; the nonspecific metabolism/homeostasis annotation does not establish a metabolic disorder.
